subject: Pricing & batching follow-up: continuous batching assumptions and token economics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Pricing & batching follow-up: continuous batching assumptions and token economics

Alex — great to meet today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can align on a target price and pilot scope.

Recap (from our call):
- Use case: Finlytics real-time insights API embedded in customer dashboards. Short prompts, structured outputs, high QPS steady stream.
- Current traffic (you mentioned): ~150M tokens/month today, expected growth to ~500M tokens/month over 12 months (see your note below).
- Latency SLO: p50 target ~200ms for generation, p95 acceptable up to ~600ms for some ops.
- Primary constraints: predictable unit economics, ability to scale bursts, and security/compliance (we'll loop in Security later).

Items we need from you (to produce a clean pricing estimate and pilot plan):
1) Confirm current monthly token volume (baseline) and 12-month forecast (you mentioned 150M -> 500M).
2) Target budget or target $/1M tokens you hope to achieve (you referenced ~$40-60/1M in the call).
3) Workload shape details: steady QPS vs. spikes (typical daily peak factor), average prompt+completion tokens per call (ballpark is fine).

Our assumptions / initial guidance for continuous batching & concurrency:
- Expected average tokens per request: 200 tokens total (120 tokens input, 80 tokens output) - please adjust if your average differs.
- Continuous batching model: for high-throughput, low-latency streams we use a short batching window (10-30ms) that aggregates many concurrent requests into a single forward. For your workload we typically see effective batch sizes of 8-16 for steady traffic and 32+ during bursts (depends on concurrency and arrival distribution).
- Concurrency: to keep p50 ~200ms we recommend targeting 8-16 concurrent in-flight requests per model replica for your workload; higher concurrency increases batching efficiency but can add tail latency.
- Unit economics (very rough first pass): at $50 / 1M tokens, 150M tokens -> $7.5k/month; 500M tokens -> $25k/month. These numbers are illustrative - final price varies by model, reserved vs hosted, and batching gains.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the three items above.
- We run a short bench: 1 week of synthetic/recorded traffic against Hosted with our continuous-batching config to measure effective batch sizes, p50/p95, and token consumption.
- Based on bench we present a committed pricing option (hosted vs. dedicated) and an expected $/1M token target.

Attachments: I attached a quick MAUP calc you can use to sanity-check numbers and our standard pricing deck.

Thanks - I can set up the bench trial with Camila and Aditya on the engineering side once you confirm the traffic numbers and budget target.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa - good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Baseline: we're at ~150M tokens/month currently (production), with an aggressive product roadmap that could bring us to ~500M tokens/month in ~9-12 months.
- Budget target: we're aiming for unit economics in the ~$40-60 / 1M tokens range. $40 is an aspirational target; $60 is acceptable if latency and reliability tradeoffs are better.
- Workload shape: traffic is fairly steady during business hours (08:00-20:00 ET) with daily peaks ~1.8x baseline. We do see short bursts during reporting windows (up to 4x for 5-10 minutes).
- Average tokens per request: roughly 180-220 total tokens (your 200-token assumption is fine).

We're happy to proceed with a hosted bench first. Can you share an estimate of the bench timelines and what telemetry we'll get? Also please send over the MAUP calc you mentioned (I didn't see attachments in my client - could you reattach?).

Alex - thanks, this is helpful. A few technical clarifications and what we'll measure in the bench: 

Technical assumptions we'll use for the bench/test:
- Model: open-architecture 7B-class model tuned for structured outputs (we'll confirm exact variant with you).
- Batch window: 10-30ms continuous batching for steady-state; we default to 20ms for initial tests.
- Effective batch sizes: expect 8-16 at your steady QPS. During short reporting bursts we often see 24-48 depending on arrival clustering.
- Concurrency per replica: start with 8 in-flight requests per replica, iterate to 16 if we need higher throughput.
- KV cache: enabled for common prefixes where applicable - this can cut compute per request significantly for repeated context.

What we'll measure in the bench (delivered in a short results doc + dashboard):
- Realized tokens consumed vs. logical tokens per end-user interaction (to capture batching/overhead).
- p50/p95 generation latency across steady-state and burst windows.
- Effective throughput and batch-size distribution over time.
- Estimated $/1M tokens under both Hosted (pay-as-you-go) and Dedicated (reserved) pricing assumptions.

Preliminary pricing note (back-of-envelope):
- If we see effective batching that yields 2x efficiency vs naive single-request runs, your $40 target becomes more achievable (because compute/token effectively halves for some ops).
- For sustained >100M tokens/month we typically recommend a Dedicated/Committed option - lower unit price in exchange for commit. For pilots we usually run Hosted with a short commit window to validate numbers.

Attachments: re-attached the MAUP calc and a one-page pricing summary.

I'll coordinate with Aditya to provision the bench environment - Marissa, can you pick 2-3 sample endpoints or recorded traffic slices Finlytics is comfortable sharing for the test?

Cheers,
Camila Reyes
